# The retina

---

![Retinal rods (green) & cones (blue)](https://i.pinimg.com/originals/9f/08/85/9f0885d4c209d5275f631ac194eb4f4b.jpg){#fig-rods-cones}

## How photoreceptors work

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Outer segment
    + Membrane disks
    + *Photopigments*
        - Sense light, trigger chemical cascade
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![@Land1999-af](https://cdn.britannica.com/44/55744-050-4F61301B/cells-cones-eye-retina-segment-rod-phototransduction.jpg)
:::
::::
    
## How photoreceptors work

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Inner segment
    + Synaptic terminal
- Light *hyperpolarizes* photoreceptor!
    + The *dark current*
- *Less* light $\rightarrow$ more NT (glutamate)!
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![@Land1999-af](https://cdn.britannica.com/44/55744-050-4F61301B/cells-cones-eye-retina-segment-rod-phototransduction.jpg)
:::
::::
    
## Retina

- Physiologically *backwards*
    + How?
- Anatomically *inside-out*
    + How?
    
## Retina

- Physiologically *backwards*
    + Dark current (more NT released in dark than light)
- Anatomically *inside-out*
    + Photoreceptors at back of eye

---

### Photoreceptors are arranged in mosaics

![Normal color vision vs. protanopic (color blind) vision; Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retinal_mosaic](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a6/ConeMosaics.jpg){#fig-cone-rod-mosaics}

---

### with different concentrations in different parts of the retina

![https://book.bionumbers.org/how-big-is-a-photoreceptor/](https://book.bionumbers.org/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/130-f2-RodCellDensity-12.png){#fig-book-bionumbers}

## Photoreceptor distribution

- Retinal periphery
  - Mostly rods
- Retinal center/fovea 
  - Mostly cones
  - ~1-2 deg of visual angle
  
---

![@UnknownUnknown-qs](https://nightsky.jpl.nasa.gov/media/images/Handy_Degrees_NSN_8961.original.jpg){#fig-visual-field-approx width="65%"}

## Consequences

- Must move eyes (or eyes/head or eyes/head/body) to position fovea on target
- Keep track of sequence of eye movements and positions over time
- Integrate sequence of samples over time

---

![@Cairo2013-hm Figure 5.6](../include/img/cairo-fig-5.6.png)



## Retinal information processing

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width=50%}

- Separate channels for
  - Achromatic (black/gray/white) info
    - Mostly rods
  - Chromatic
    - Mostly cones
    - Short, medium, long wavelength types

:::
::: {.column width=50%}

- Pixels/photoreceptor analogy
  - ~120 M rods + ~ 5 M cones (125 M) 
  - vs. professional cameras with 100 M pixels

:::
::::

## Retinal information processing

- Point by point, topographic (map-like) 2D image of 3D world
- Non-uniform resolution (center >> periphery)
- yields focused image except...

## Color perception

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Perceived color a function of activity in "R", "G", and "B" photoreceptors
:::
::: {.column width=50%}

:::
::::

## Color vision anomalies

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Absence of or anomalies in photoreceptors
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![https://bluefinvision.com/ishihara-colour-blind-test-online/](https://bluefinvision.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/eye-tests-ishihara-colour-blind-test.webp){#fig-ishihara width="55%"}
:::
::::

## Types

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=40%}
- Protanopia (impaired R/long wavelength)
- Deuteranopia (impaired G/medium wavelength)
- Tritanopia (impaired B/short wavelength)
:::
::: {.column width=60%}
![https://www.color-blindness.com/protanopia-red-green-color-blindness/](https://www.color-blindness.com/wp-content/images/Protanopia-Color-Spectrum.jpg){#fig-color-vision-anomolies}
:::
::::

## What's a reddish-green look like?

## Explanation

![](../include/img/RGBOpponent.gif){#fig-color-opponency fig-align="center"}

## Opponent processing

- Black vs. white (achromatic)
- Long (<span class="red">red</span>) vs. Medium (<span class="green">green</span>) wavelength cones
- (Long + Medium) vs. Short (<span class="blue">blue</span>) cones
- Can't really see reddish-green or bluish-yellow

## Color opponency

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Sensitivity curves for medium and long wavelength cones overlap
- Color opponency "pushes" signals apart
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![http://hyperphysics.phy-astr.gsu.edu/hbase/vision/colcon.html](http://hyperphysics.phy-astr.gsu.edu/hbase/vision/imgvis/colcon.png)
:::
::::
